features.text: Patient reports feeling a lot of the same pain as when he had kidney stones about two years ago.
Pain is located on the right side of the back and has shifted to the left side.
Pain has been present for the last four days.
Pain initially came and went but has been constant for the last 48 hours and is described as pretty bad.
Patient has taken Tylenol for the pain, but it does not seem to help.
Patient reports some discoloration of the urine, though it is hard to detect.
Patient experiences dizziness and lightheadedness during physical exertion, such as climbing stairs or running to catch a bus, along with increased abdominal pain.
Patient has been diligent about taking prescribed medications.
Patient has been ordering take-out and fast food due to difficulty moving around because of pain.
Patient has some body aches due to favoring the back while walking.
Physical exam reveals tenderness on the right-hand side (CDA tenderness) and tenderness on palpation of the right lower quadrant of the abdomen.
Creatinine levels are slightly elevated, suggesting possible obstruction due to a kidney stone.
Abdominal x-rays show a possible kidney stone.
Patient needs a refill of medication.
Patient prefers to have food delivered to avoid physical exertion.
